summary: Defines a Management Information Base for managing the radio frequency interfaces of systems compliant with DOCSIS 2.0, the cable-modem standard, using SNMP. It covers cable modems and the cable modem termination systems they connect to. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: A cable network carries data over coax in the same frequency ranges that carry television. DOCSIS is the set of rules that let a cable modem send data upstream and receive it downstream. This document defines the standard objects that a management program uses to inspect and control that radio equipment: the channels and their bandwidth, the signal quality, the modulation formats in use, and the queues that decide whose data goes up next.

subtitle: A standard SNMP view of the radio interfaces of cable modems and the head-end equipment that drives them.

tldr.problem: Cable operators need to see and control the radio side of their network: the channels, the signal levels, the modulations and the queues. DOCSIS equipment did not have a standard way to expose that over SNMP.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines a MIB module, DOCS-IF-MIB, with three groups of objects: what both ends share, what only the cable modem has, and what only the head-end has. It also says how the new objects fit into the general Interfaces MIB.
tldr.outcome: This revises and obsoletes RFC 2670, adding the DOCSIS 2.0 capabilities and the European spectrum lineup, and it includes a mechanism for changing an upstream channel's settings without taking the link out of service.

today: RFC 4546 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted, so it remains the current MIB module for DOCSIS radio frequency interfaces. It revised and obsoleted RFC 2670, and it was later updated by RFC 9141.

sections.title: The Internet-Standard Management Framework
sections.content:
Managed objects are accessed via a virtual information store, termed the Management Information Base. MIB objects are generally accessed through the Simple Network Management Protocol. Objects in the MIB are defined using the mechanisms defined in the Structure of Management Information. This memo specifies a MIB module that is compliant to SMIv2, which is described in STD 58, RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580.

The memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base for use with network management protocols in the Internet community. In particular, it defines a set of managed objects for SNMP based management of the Radio Frequency interfaces for systems compliant with the Data Over Cable Service Interface Specifications.
sections.plainLanguage: The document defines a table of readable and writable values that a management program can fetch and set over SNMP, in the same way that earlier management standards did for routers and for interfaces in general.

sections.title: The Vocabulary of a Cable Network
sections.content:
A CM, or Cable Modem, acts as a slave station in a DOCSIS-compliant cable data system. A CMTS, or Cable Modem Termination System, is a generic term covering a cable bridge or cable router in a head-end. It acts as the master station, is the only station that transmits downstream, and controls the scheduling of upstream transmissions by its associated cable modems. The head-end is the origination point in most cable systems of the subscriber video signals, and generally also the location of the CMTS equipment. Downstream is the direction from the head-end towards the subscriber, and upstream is the direction from the subscriber towards the head-end.

A channel is a specific frequency allocation with an RF medium, specified by channel width in Hertz and by center frequency. Within the US cable systems, upstream channels are generally allocated from the 5-42 MHz range while downstream channels are generally allocated from the 50-750 MHz range, depending on the capabilities of the given system. The typical broadcast channel width in the US is 6 MHz. For European cable systems, the upper edge of upstream channel allocations varies between 25 MHz and 65 MHz, and the lower edge of downstream channel allocations varies between 47 MHz and 87.5 MHz, with a typical broadcast channel width in Europe of 8 MHz.

A mini-slot is an interval of time allocated by the CMTS to a given cable modem for that modem to transmit in the upstream direction. A MAC Packet is a DOCSIS PDU, and the Data Packet is the payload portion of it. QPSK and QAM are particular modulation schemes on an RF medium, with QAM usually expressed with a number indicating the size of the modulation constellation, for example 16 QAM. A codeword is a characteristic of the forward error correction scheme used above the RF media layer. dBmV is a measure of RF signal voltage amplitude, whose power level is determined by the characteristic impedance; a zero dB signal power is equivalent to 48.75 dBmV signal amplitude in a 75 Ohm system.
sections.plainLanguage: The glossary separates the two ends: the cable modem in the house, and the equipment at the head-end that sends data downstream and decides when each modem may speak upstream. It also fixes the frequency plan, because the upstream and downstream bands are different in different countries.

sections.title: The Three Groups of Objects
sections.content:
The MIB module provides the objects required for the management of DOCSIS-compliant Cable Modem and Cable Modem Termination System RF interfaces, and is derived in part from the parameters and protocols described in the DOCSIS 2.0 specification. It is structured as three groups.

The first, docsIfBaseObjects, holds management information pertinent to both the cable modem and the cable modem termination system. It contains docsIfDownstreamChannelTable, describing the existing downstream channels for a CMTS and the received downstream channel for a CM; docsIfUpstreamChannelTable, describing the existing upstream channels for a CMTS and the current upstream transmission channel for a CM; docsIfQosProfileTable, describing the valid Quality of Service profiles for the cable data system; docsIfSignalQualityTable, used to monitor RF signal quality characteristics of received signals; and docsIfDocsisBaseCapability, used to indicate the highest level of DOCSIS version a cable device can support.

The second, docsIfCmObjects, holds management information pertinent to the cable modem only. It contains docsIfCmMacTable, used to monitor the DOCSIS MAC interface and which can be considered an extension to the ifEntry; docsIfCmStatusTable, maintaining status objects and counters for cable modems, with a comparable table at the CMTS, docsIfCmtsCmStatusTable; and docsIfCmServiceTable, describing the upstream service queues available at this CM, with a comparable table at the CMTS, docsIfCmtsServiceEntry.

The third, docsIfCmtsObjects, holds management information pertinent to the cable modem termination system only. It contains docsIfCmtsMacTable, describing the attributes of each CMTS MAC interface; docsIfCmtsStatusTable, providing aggregated counters that roll up values and events on the underlying sub-interfaces; docsIfCmtsCmStatusTable, holding information about known cable modems on the system serviced by this CMTS; docsIfCmtsServiceTable, giving access to information about upstream service queues; docsIfCmtsModulationTable, which allows control over the modulation profiles for RF channels; docsIfCmtsMacToCmTable, allowing fast access into the CM table via a MAC address; docsIfCmtsChannelUtilizationTable, providing statistical load usage data for attached upstream and downstream physical channels; and the downstream and upstream channel counter tables.
sections.plainLanguage: The objects are sorted by who they describe. Some tables make sense at either end, such as the list of channels. Some only make sense at the head-end, such as how many modems are on each channel and how busy that channel is. Some only make sense at the modem, such as the signal quality it is receiving.

sections.title: How the RF Objects Fit the Interfaces MIB
sections.content:
The document clarifies the relationship of this MIB module to the Interfaces MIB. In the layering model, an instance of ifEntry exists for each RF downstream interface, for each RF upstream interface, for each upstream logical channel, and for each RF MAC layer. The ifStackTable MUST be implemented to identify the relationships among sub-interfaces.

The example given is a CMTS MAC interface with one downstream and two upstream interfaces, where the RF MAC interface is layered on top of the downstream and upstream interfaces, and the RF upstream interface is layered on top of an upstream logical channel. The assignment of index values given is 2 for the CATV MAC layer with ifType docsCableMaclayer, 3 for the CATV downstream interface with ifType docsCableDownstream, 4 and 5 for the CATV upstream interfaces with ifType docsCableUpstream, and 6 to 9 for the CATV upstream channels with ifType docsCableUpstreamChannel.

The same interface model can also be used in Telephony or Telco Return systems. A pure Telco Return system would not have upstream cable channels, only downstream cable channels, and systems supporting both Telco Return and cable upstream channels can use the model without modification. Telco Return upstream channel management is outside the scope of the document. This medium does not support virtual circuits, and the ifTestTable and ifRcvAddressTable are optional for DOCSIS implementations but are not specifically influenced by the RF MIB.
sections.plainLanguage: The new objects are not a separate world. They hang off the ordinary interface table, so the same stack of interfaces that a router has also describes a cable head-end. The document gives the exact index numbering to use, so that tools can tell which row is which.

sections.title: Offline Upstream Parameter Handling
sections.content:
This section describes the offline configuration of the DOCSIS 2.0 upstream logical interface parameters. The purpose of the feature is to guarantee that upstream logical interface parameters, such as modulation profile, channel type, mini-slot size and SCDMA attributes, are consistent prior to committing changes to an active upstream logical interface. The mechanism can reduce possible downtime of the upstream interface by minimizing SNMP SET operations to in-service upstream interfaces. It is supported by CMTSs and is not applicable to cable modems.

The mechanism uses three upstream channel MIB objects. docsIfUpChannelStatus is the RowStatus object for the creation of temporary interfaces in the upstream interface table, and a temporary entry is used to modify, validate and commit the upstream parameters of a physical interface. docsIfUpChannelCloneFrom associates a physical interface with a temporary interface for the purpose of updating the upstream parameters of the physical interface. docsIfUpChannelUpdate is the commit object that transfers the validated upstream parameters from the temporary interface to the physical interface.

The operation runs as follows. A temporary interface is created in which docsIfUpChannelStatus is set to createAndWait, which turns the new create entry status to notReady. A SET to docsIfUpChannelCloneFrom in the temporary interface to the physical interface ifIndex value creates the association of the physical interface to the temporary interface and copies the original upstream parameters from the physical interface to the temporary interface, which turns its status to notInService. The operator then modifies the temporary interface parameters to the desired values. At this point, a SET to active to the RowStatus of the temporary interface is successful if all parameters in the temporary interface are valid for the associated physical interface; otherwise the temporary entry remains with status notInService and the SET returns the error commitFailed. When the temporary interface status is active, a SET to docsIfUpChannelUpdate to true transfers the temporary interface parameter values to the physical interface. After completion of the update operations, the temporary interface is destroyed by setting docsIfUpChannelStatus to destroy.
sections.plainLanguage: Changing the settings of a live upstream channel is risky, because a half-applied change could break the link. The document gives a safe recipe: work on a copy, check that the new settings are acceptable, and only then swap them in, all over ordinary SNMP SET operations.

sections.title: What Changed from RFC 2670
sections.content:
The MIB module in this document has been developed to accommodate DOCSIS 2.0 devices and their system capabilities. It is an update to RFC 2670 with the additional incorporation of the DOCSIS 2.0 and Euro-DOCSIS specification requirements.

The MIB objects defined in RFC 2670 have been maintained. In some cases new MIB objects have been created with identical functionality but greater capacity, that is, 32 to 64 bits. In these situations, both the original 32 bit objects and the new 64 bit objects must be implemented.

The revision note for this version lists the changes: usage of ifType 205 for upstream logical channels, addition of downstream and upstream utilization counters, additional statistics per upstream interface, the upstream channel offline configuration mechanism, MIB support for new DOCSIS 2.0 modulation attributes, Euro-DOCSIS downstream interleave values, and adjustments to the RFC 2670 definitions based on the MIB review guidelines from the IETF Operations and Management Area.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier MIB is still there. This version adds what DOCSIS 2.0 and the European spectrum plan need, and where a counter grew too large for 32 bits, a wider version was added alongside the old one rather than replacing it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
This MIB module relates to a system that will provide metropolitan public internet access. Improper manipulation of the MIB objects represented by this module may result in denial of service to a large number of end-users.

There are a number of management objects defined in this MIB that have a MAX-ACCESS clause of read-write or read-create. The CMTS is the controller of most of the parameters of the DOCSIS RFI interface, so write access to the CMTS MIB objects may compromise the end-user's services. Objects in the docsIfBasicGroupv2, if SET maliciously, could result in a denial of service; particularly, SETs to objects in docsIfDownstreamChannelTable, docsIfUpstreamChannelTable, docsIfCmtsModulationTable and docsIfQosProfileTable can alter negatively the physical and link layer parameters of upstream and downstream channels. The object docsIfCmtsServiceAdminStatus, when SET maliciously by an attacker to disabled or destroyed, will interrupt the service of the corresponding cable modem. In the CM case, the only read-write object of this module is docsIfCmRangingTimeout, and the rest of the CM-required objects are read-only.

Some of the readable objects may also be considered sensitive. Read access to the objects in the tables docsIfCmStatusTable, docsIfSignalQualityTable, docsIfCmtsCmStatusTable, docsIfCmtsChannelUtilizationTable, docsIfCmtsDownChannelCounterTable and docsIfCmtsUpChannelCounterTable could reveal information about the cable modems' distribution among the upstream and downstream channels and their performance, which could be used to gain access to a different tiered service offer. The table docsIfCmtsCmStatusTable also contains the MAC and IP addresses of the cable modems, which can be used for theft of service.

SNMP versions prior to SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. Deployment of SNMP versions prior to SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. Instead, it is RECOMMENDED to deploy SNMPv3 and enable cryptographic security, and it is then the operator's responsibility to ensure that the SNMP entity giving access to an instance of this module is properly configured to give access only to principals with legitimate rights.
sections.plainLanguage: The head-end controls almost everything here, so a management write at the wrong moment can take a whole neighbourhood offline. Even reading is sensitive, because the tables show which modems are on which channel, how well each is doing, and where they live on the network.

sections.title: Management Interoperability of DOCSIS 1.0, 1.1 and 2.0
sections.content:
The MIB module contained in this document updates RFC 2670, primarily to handle the management requirements of the DOCSIS RF Interface of DOCSIS 2.0. RFC 2670 contains the DOCSIS RF Interface management requirements for DOCSIS 1.0 and DOCSIS 1.1.

The management requirements of Class of Service, which is DOCSIS 1.0, pertaining to RFC 2670 are the same as this document update and are contained in the tables docsIfQosProfileTable, docsIfCmServiceTable and docsIfCmtsServiceTable. DOCSIS 1.1 and DOCSIS 2.0 Quality of Service management requirements are defined in the DOCSIS management specifications respectively.
sections.plainLanguage: The module has to work with equipment of three different generations of the DOCSIS standard, and the way it does that is by keeping the old objects and adding new ones. The quality of service tables are the ones shared across the versions.

items.desc: Simultaneous support of the TDMA and A-TDMA modes.

items.title: docsIfBaseObjects
items.text: Objects that apply to both the cable modem and the cable modem termination system.

items.title: docsIfCmObjects
items.text: Objects that apply to the cable modem only, such as its status counters and its own service queues.

items.title: docsIfCmtsObjects
items.text: Objects that apply to the cable modem termination system only, such as the modem list, channel utilization and modulation control.

viz.caption: THE SAFE WAY TO CHANGE AN UPSTREAM CHANNEL

items.title: Create a temporary entry
items.text: Set docsIfUpChannelStatus to createAndWait, which leaves the new row as notReady.

items.title: Clone the live interface
items.text: A SET to docsIfUpChannelCloneFrom copies the current parameters into the temporary row, which becomes notInService.

items.title: Change the parameters
items.text: The operator edits the temporary row to the wanted values.

items.title: Validate
items.text: Setting the row to active succeeds only if every parameter is valid; otherwise the SET returns commitFailed.

items.title: Commit and clean up
items.text: A SET to docsIfUpChannelUpdate of true copies the values over, and the temporary row is then destroyed.

viz.caption: WHAT THIS VERSION ADDS TO THE EARLIER MIB

cells: Usage of ifType 205 for upstream logical channels
MIB support for new DOCSIS 2.0 modulation attributes

items.title: Writes at the head-end
items.text: The CMTS controls most of the RF parameters, so write access to its objects may compromise the end-user's services.

items.title: Writes at the modem
items.text: The only read-write object required of a cable modem is docsIfCmRangingTimeout.

items.title: Readable information
items.text: The modem status and channel utilization tables reveal how modems are distributed and performing, and the CM status table holds MAC and IP addresses.

items.title: SNMPv3
items.text: Deployment of SNMP versions prior to SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED; SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy is.
